case.description: Develop an analysis workflow to reconcile two synthetic reports of a batch transfer exercise. A reviewer must determine which discrepancies can be resolved from bounded records and which require a targeted follow-up request.
case.valued_outcome: For each of twelve batch identifiers, produce a reconciled quantity or explicit bounded disagreement, cite supporting records, and issue at most three follow-up requests that each name a missing field or record.
hard_constraints: Never silently drop duplicate or unmatched rows.
Use only the supplied unit-conversion table.
Do not infer missing quantities from neighboring batches.
Complete the review within sixty minutes.
resources: Two synthetic reports with thirty rows each, twelve batch identifiers, quantities, units and status fields.
Eight amendment records with explicit superseded-row references.
A table specifying that one fictional unit U equals five fictional units V, plus a status dictionary and report cutoff times.
Spreadsheet or local script environment and sixty minutes of reviewer time.
observations: Seven batches agree after applying the supplied conversion.
Three identifiers each occur twice in one report.

Awkward observation: the newer report includes an amendment whose effective time precedes both cutoffs, while the older report already includes its replacement quantity under a different row identifier.

Twenty extra minutes to compare two workflow variants using resolved-batch counts, unsupported definite claims and follow-up-request counts.

Feasible probe resources must be source-supported; no physical/human measured success inferred. Shared seed/concern can establish overlap but is not attributed as treatment discovery.
contract.protected_retention: Relation and full prediction/probe including all rivals, directional comparisons, challenge/defeat and capacity/resource caveats; uncertainty and declared fit. Summaries may have six post cards per two raw cards; evaluate all post IDs, every raw source and exact lineage. Faithful inherited raw errors are separate from new summary assertions. Park/reject disposition may preserve protected content in its reason; absent targets alone do not prove loss.
contract.unit_contract: Apply only the assigned per-unit instruction; ordinary/generic controls are not required to perform the treatment. Honest no viable opening is a valid execution result, not a discovery or zero-valued missing assessment. Distinguish raw completeness from summary completeness.
contract.family_assessment: Judge all explicit archive/candidate pairs from causal operation, carrier/path and prediction/test, not words. family_confirmed only if relevant comparisons resolve. Same-family overlap prevents exclusivity even if comparator fit/contract is partial. Preserve uncertain links and no forced transitive merges.

openings.claim: A batch can have a defensible quantity while record identity remains unresolved, if every supported revision interpretation yields that same quantity.
openings.delta: Change the decision dependency from exact cross-report row identity to quantity invariance across explicitly documented revision interpretations. Carry identity uncertainty separately in a row-accounting ledger. Explicit supersession links remain authoritative; matching converted quantities never establish an alias by themselves.
openings.prediction: Against the nearest rival, a register requiring identical row identifiers before recognizing agreement, the awkward amendment may permit quantity agreement with an explicit identity caveat and fewer follow-ups. Disturbed references or undefined statuses should widen disagreement or trigger a named request, rather than produce unsupported certainty.
openings.probe: Using the supplied copies, run the identity-register baseline and invariance workflow on both versions. Allocate ten minutes to setup/freeze and twenty-five minutes per variant, including its disturbed final pass. Freeze twelve batch outcomes, supporting row dispositions and at most three named requests for each version; then use the extra twenty minutes to open the key and compare resolved counts, unsupported definite claims and request counts. Defeat the hypothesis if apparent agreement conceals distinct keyed quantities, unsupported claims increase, or review exceeds sixty minutes.
assumptions: The supplied status dictionary and amendment content must support a bounded set of quantity interpretations without inventing aggregation rules; their actual contents are unprovided here.

Capacity is sixty rows and eight amendments in the stipulated spreadsheet/script environment. If interpretation enumeration cannot finish within the allocation, retain explicit bounded disagreements; the time cap alone does not establish feasibility.

No missing quantity is reconstructed. Every duplicate and unmatched row receives an explicit disposition. Requests name the missing superseded-row reference, undefined-code dictionary entry, or authoritative cross-report row mapping, as applicable.

artifact.assessment: A hypothetical discriminating test, not deployment or measured improvement. Equal quantities alone cannot settle whether duplicate records represent separate transfers; that uncertainty limits definite reconciliation.

openings.claim: Reconcile revision state before comparing report quantities; report recency alone cannot establish replacement identity.
openings.delta: Change the comparison dependency to a row-preserving revision ledger: retain all sixty rows, link only explicit superseded references, record effective times against cutoffs, and normalize only with U=5V. Equal quantities under different identifiers remain candidate equivalence, never proof.
openings.prediction: Against a latest-report-wins rival, this ledger should expose the awkward cross-identifier replacement as supported identity or bounded disagreement, with fewer unsupported definite claims. The missing reference and undefined status should propagate uncertainty rather than erase rows.
openings.probe: Within the shared sixty-minute review, produce twelve cited outcomes and annotate the rival's alternative choices on amendment-linked and duplicate rows. Freeze outputs, then use the supplied twenty-minute comparison and sealed key to score resolutions, unsupported claims, and requests. Defeat: equal or greater unsupported claims, or no distinct rival choices. Capacity condition: all sixty rows and eight amendments must be accounted for; unfinished analysis becomes explicit disagreement. Timing remains unmeasured.
assumptions: Explicit references and the supplied dictionary may support identity; absent references or undefined codes do not.
No neighboring-batch imputation or additional conversion is permitted.

openings.claim: Request selection by shared missing evidence may cover more unresolved batches within three requests.
openings.delta: Replace one-request-per-batch selection with a dependency map from unresolved batches to exact missing fields or records. Select at most three requests; retain cited bounded disagreements for every uncovered batch.
openings.prediction: Versus choosing the first three unresolved batches, shared-dependency selection should cover more batches per request only when unresolved batches actually share missing evidence.
openings.probe: Using the frozen R1 ledger, enumerate both request sets during the supplied comparison period and count batches whose named evidence gaps each set covers. This tests coverage, not actual resolution without replies. Defeat: no shared gaps or no coverage advantage. Resource condition: each request must identify a concrete missing field or record; undefined-code meaning cannot be invented.
assumptions: Shared gaps are possible, not supplied observations.
Follow-up replies are not available probe resources.

Let M mean all superseded-row references are present and B mean the valued outcome is met. B does not imply M: explicit bounded disagreement can satisfy B when M is false. M alone also does not establish B.
openings.delta: Remove the global dependency on repairing every superseded-row reference. Carry a per-batch ledger retaining every original, duplicate, unmatched and amendment row. Apply explicit links where available; preserve recorded alternatives where the missing link prevents selection. For the awkward amendment, record possible double counting without assuming equal quantities prove identical events. Use only the supplied conversion and dictionary; infer no missing quantity.
openings.prediction: A source-compatible counterexample is the disturbed copy producing twelve cited outputs, including bounded disagreements for affected batches, while the missing reference remains absent. The nearest rival requires repairing that reference before completing linked-record reconciliation. Removal should avoid that dependency without increasing unsupported definite claims; resolved-batch gains are uncertain.
openings.probe: On the two supplied copies, compare the ledger workflow against ordinary specific-record amendment linking with a completeness gate. Freeze outputs before opening the sealed key. Within the extra twenty minutes compare resolved-batch counts, unsupported definite claims and request counts, including whether missing-reference effects remain local. Each workflow retains the sixty-minute review limit. No follow-up answer is assumed.
assumptions: Recorded alternatives and the missing selection relationship can express a bounded disagreement without inventing quantities.
Reserve field-specific requests for the removed superseded-row reference and the undefined status dictionary entry; permit at most one further missing-field or record request.

Defeat: the ledger loses a row, asserts an unsupported resolution, cannot produce twelve cited outcomes within sixty minutes, or needs more than three requests. Actual record structure and reviewer capacity remain untested.

openings.claim: Reconcile each batch through a row-preserving evidence ledger and explicit alternative interpretations of ambiguous replacement identity.
openings.delta: Change the dependency from report recency or quantity equality to recorded supersession, dictionary meaning and cutoff applicability. Carry every original row, including duplicates and unmatched rows, into the ledger; apply only U=5V. An older replacement under another identifier remains distinct unless supplied evidence establishes identity.
openings.prediction: Against a conservative explicit-reference-only rival, enumerating supported interpretations can resolve a quantity when every interpretation yields it, while exposing disagreement when replacement identity changes the result. It may resolve no additional batches; equal converted quantities alone will never establish identity.
openings.probe: Within twenty extra minutes, run both workflow variants on the clean and disturbed copies using a spreadsheet or local script. Give each variant the same sixty-minute review cap; freeze twelve batch decisions, citations and requests before opening the sealed key. Compare resolved-batch counts, unsupported definite claims and request counts. Inspect whether any claimed invariant survives the removed reference and undefined status.
assumptions: All numeric reconciliation follows only aggregation meanings actually supplied by the status dictionary; no missing quantity comes from neighboring batches.
Reserve review minutes 0-15 for row capture/conversion, 15-40 for amendment and cutoff checks, and 40-60 for decisions and requests.
At the deadline, retain unresolved alternatives with cited candidate quantities and unresolved fields; an undefined status cannot support a definite total.

Issue at most three targeted requests: the missing superseded-row reference, the undefined status dictionary entry, and, if necessary, the record linking differently identified replacement rows. Further uncertainty remains explicitly reported.

Defeat conditions include unsupported identity links, missed surviving rows, or alternative enumeration exceeding reviewer capacity. Stop enumeration and report bounded disagreement; the cap alone supplies no evidence of informativeness.

artifact.assessment: This is a proposed workflow and comparative probe, not a measured result or deployment. Feasibility of exhaustive interpretation checks within sixty minutes remains uncertain; definitive output requires complete supporting records.
